styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: The Kremlin, Red Square and the metro palaces.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Cathedrals, Soviet landmarks and war memorials.

styles.label: Art
styles.blurb: Tretyakov, Pushkin and the Garage galleries.

stays.why: Central and walkable. Close to Red Square, the Bolshoi and good restaurants. Metro everywhere.
Steps from Red Square and the Kremlin. Quiet lanes, easy metro links.
Lively pedestrian street, cafés and shops. Walk to the Kremlin in about 20 minutes.
Quieter, greener area near the Cathedral of Christ the Saviour and Gorky Park.

food: Try Russian classics: borscht, pelmeni dumplings, blini and syrniki pancakes.
Look for stolovaya canteens for cheap, filling lunches; prices vary, check the day's menu.
Georgian food is everywhere and good: khachapuri bread and khinkali dumplings.
Coffee and pastry culture is strong in the centre; many cafés open early.
Book popular restaurants ahead for weekend evenings. Tipping of about 10% is common.
more_time: Add a day for a country estate or monastery outside the centre; check opening days and transport first.
Art lovers can swap a museum for a gallery afternoon in the former factory districts.
In warm months, spend an evening on a river cruise or a walk in Gorky Park.

recommend.why: Three nights covers the Kremlin, Red Square, the big museums and the metro stations without rushing.

month_notes: January: cold, highs near -5°C. Pack layers and warm boots; days are short.
February: still cold, highs near -3°C. Fewer rain days than January.
March: slowly warms to about 2°C. Icy underfoot; watch your step.
April: milder, highs near 11°C. Expect about 10 rain days; bring a jacket.
May: pleasant at about 18°C. Good month for walking and parks.
June: warm, highs near 23°C. Long daylight hours; a great month to visit.
July: warmest month, about 24°C, but the wettest with around 14 rain days.
August: warm at about 23°C and drier than July. Good for outdoor sights.
September: mild at about 17°C. Comfortable for museums and city walks.
October: cooler, highs near 9°C. Around 12 rain days; take an umbrella.
November: cold at about 2°C. Short days and grey skies.
December: cold, highs near -2°C. Festive lights but pack for ice and snow.

climate_guide.summary: Continental climate with cold winters and warm summers. Rain falls in every month, so pack a layer and an umbrella.

items.title: Best time: May to September
items.text: Highs of 17–24°C and long days. Ideal for walking, parks and the river.

items.title: Winter is long and cold
items.text: December to February highs sit near -2 to -5°C. Wear a warm coat, hat, gloves and boots.

items.title: Rain in every month
items.text: Expect 8–14 rain days monthly. July and December are wettest; August is driest.

items.title: Icy streets in winter
items.text: Pavements can be slippery from November to March. Choose shoes with grip.

items.title: Short winter days
items.text: Daylight is limited in December and January. Plan indoor sights and start early.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Summer: light clothes and a rain jacket. Winter: heavy coat, thermals, hat, gloves and waterproof boots.

transit.best: Metro for almost everything; it is fast, cheap and the stations are sights themselves.

modes.text: Runs about 05:30–01:00. Fast and cheap; a Troika card cuts fares. Stations are attractions in themselves.
Buses, trolleybuses and trams fill the gaps. A Troika card cuts fares.
Yandex Go is the main app. Taxis are metered, but agree the price first.
Driving in the centre is slow and parking is costly. Use park-and-ride instead.
Central streets are walkable. Bike lanes are limited and winter is icy.
No useful ferry service in the city.
